comments: # 'review' can tell those changes from the executor's. They still go into
# 'tests' is later in THIS loop, so it means the PREVIOUS
# It neither switches nor creates a branch, and it starts from the working tree
# Records what was already uncommitted before the run touched anything, so
# and review in a cycle, then commit on sign-off. Run it again for the next
# as it is: changes already uncommitted there become part of its commit.
# findings/feedback — all three are simply skipped, on the
# first pass of each, when there is nothing yet to read.
# iteration's log; 'review' and 'sign-off' are later siblings
# made — on the branch you are on, plan, implement, gate on tests passing,
# of the OUTER loops, so they mean the previous ROUND's
# small step on the same branch. Reference: docs/design.md
# this run's commit.
